column1: 3:1|Woe to the city of blood!\nIt is full of lies and plunder;\nthe prey never runs out.|Keeps blood-city indictment and continuing predation as images rather than abstract wrongdoing.
3:2|Whips crack, wheels rumble,\nhorses gallop, chariots bounce.|Lets the Hebrew sound-and-motion fragments drive the battle scene.

3:3|Horsemen charge, swords flash,
spears glitter!
So many slain, heaps of corpses,
bodies without end—
they stumble over the bodies.|Preserves the accumulating bodies and follows the read form of stumble without suppressing the written form in the binding.

3:4|All because of the countless prostitutions
of the alluring prostitute,
the mistress of sorcery,
who sells nations through her prostitution
and peoples through her sorcery.|Retains the violent sexual and magical depiction of the imperial city and both repetitions.

3:5|“Look, I am against you,” declares the LORD of Armies.
“I will lift your skirts over your face
and show the nations your nakedness,
the kingdoms your disgrace.|Makes the speaker explicit while preserving threatened sexual humiliation.
3:6|I will throw filth on you,\ntreat you with contempt,\nand make you a spectacle.|Retains all three actions without softening their degrading force.

3:7|Everyone who sees you will run away and say,\n‘Nineveh is ruined! Who will mourn for her?’\nWhere can I find anyone to comfort you?”|Distinguishes the onlookers’ speech from the returning question addressed to Nineveh.

3:8|Are you better than No-amon,
seated among the Nile’s channels,
with water all around her,
the sea her defense,
water her wall?|Keeps the ancient place-name and aquatic defense rather than replacing the image with a modern geography claim.
3:9|Cush and Egypt were her boundless strength;\nPut and the Libyans were your helpers.|Preserves the source switch from her to your rather than silently regularizing it.

3:10|Yet she too was carried away into captivity.
Her little children were dashed to pieces
at every street corner.
Lots were cast for her honored men,
and all her great men were bound in chains.|States harm to children and the enslavement of leaders explicitly.
3:11|You too will become drunk;\nyou will go into hiding.\nYou too will seek shelter from the enemy.|Keeps the two you-too parallels and the intoxication image.

3:12|All your fortresses are fig trees
with early-ripe fruit.
Shake them, and the figs fall
straight into the eater’s mouth.|Unfolds the extended simile into readable lines without adding a siege explanation.

3:13|Look at your people: women in your midst!\nYour land’s gates stand wide open to your enemies;\nfire has eaten through their bars.|Preserves the gendered taunt and gate-bar image; its ancient insult is not converted into a claim about women today.

3:14|Draw water for the siege!
Strengthen your fortresses!
Step into the mud, tread the clay,
take hold of the brick mold!|Retains the urgent commands and concrete brickmaking work.

3:15|There the fire will consume you;
the sword will cut you down,
devouring you like a locust.
Multiply like the locust!
Multiply like the swarm!|Preserves the taunt’s repeated multiplication and consuming insect imagery.

3:16|You made your merchants more numerous\nthan the stars of heaven.\nThe locust strips the land and flies away.|Keeps the comparison of commercial multitude and departing locust, noting the stripping/shedding ambiguity.

3:17|Your officials are like locusts,
your marshals like swarms
settling on walls on a cold day.
When the sun rises, they flee;
no one knows where they have gone.|Clarifies the collective insect picture without assigning modern ranks to uncertain titles.

3:18|Your shepherds sleep, king of Assyria;
your nobles lie at rest.
Your people are scattered over the mountains,
and no one gathers them.|Retains shepherd language for leaders and the ominous sleep/rest parallel.

3:19|There is no relief for your fracture;
your wound is fatal.
Everyone who hears the news about you claps their hands.
For who has not suffered your endless cruelty?|Keeps the final rhetorical question grounded in the empire’s repeated harm.
